Table 1 from the document "Perspectives on the relationship between materials chemistry and roll-to-roll electrode manufacturing for high-energy lithium-ion batteries" (ensm-2020) is as follows:

| Process Technology or Cell Chemistry Modification | Areal Capacity Improvement (mAh/cm^2) | Calendered Electrode Thickness (μm) | Specific Capacity Improvement (mAh/g) | Estimated Energy Density Improvement (Wh/kg) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Section 4 – Water-Based Processing of Cathodes (i.e. NMC 532) | 6–8 | 110–150 | 160 | 225–250 |
| Section 5 – Water-Based Processing of Si/C Anodes (N:P ¼ 1.1) | 6.6–8.8 | 45–60 | 854 (15 wt% Si) | 250–275 |
| Section 6 – Low-Co/Ni-Rich Cathodes (i.e. NMC 811) | 6–8 | 90–125 | 190 | 275–300 |
| Section 7 – Co-Free NFA | 4–6 | 65–100 | 180 | 250–275 |
| Section 8 – Coating Parameter and Drying Protocols | NA | 45–150 | NA | 220-240^a |
| Section 9 – Ultra-High-Speed (Thick) Electrode Processing | 8–8.8 | Anode – 110 | Anode – 854 | 325-350^b |
| Section 10- Ultra-Fast Formation Cycling | NA | NA | 150^a | 260-280^a,b |

The technology with the largest estimated energy density improvement is Section 9 – Ultra-High-Speed (Thick) Electrode Processing, with an estimated energy density improvement of 325-350 Wh/kg.
